newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA MOBILE PHONE NETWORK RAISES PRICES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA MOBILE PHONE NETWORK RAISES PRICES.

text.p: Bulgarian cellular telephone operator Mobikom, 49 percent owned by Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc, raised rates on Friday to keep up with the sinking local currency and to support expansion.
Mobikom general manager John Munnery told a news conference that because of inflation tariffs had fallen to well below the level needed to sustain the business.
"If we are charging six cents a minute when we should be charging 30 cents a minute, our revenues have fallen to one fifith of what they should be," he added.
Bugaria's Committee for Post and Telecommunications approved a 240 percent increase in force from Friday, said Munnery.
Despite the increase, Bulgaria will still have the lowest rates in eastern Europe, where the average rate is 39 cents a minute.
Munnery said he hoped the committee would approve a new pricing policy under which the rates could be adjusted to the lev's volatility on two-week basis.
Bulgaria's grave economic crisis has pushed the lev into a freefall. The lev collapsed to 3,200 to the dollar on Friday from 600 at the beginning of the year and 75 a year ago.
Inflation for January alone is estimated at more than 50 percent.

Mobikom, set up in 1992, is building up Bulgaria's major mobile cellular telephone system and plans to cover some 70 percent of the country's territory by year-end. The network covers more than 40 towns with 27,000 subscribers for the cellular service and 3,000 for the paging service.
Munnery was optimistic on expanding business in Bulgaria despite the economic chaos caused by delayed reform and economic mismanagement.
"Provided we get reasonable tariffs, we shall be investing up to 10 million more dollars in the network this year," said Munnery.
The major part of that investment will be used to set up a new mobile telephone exchange in the Black Sea port of Varna, making it Mobicom's second centre after Sofia.

In the three years of operation the company has paid nearly $20 million in taxes and hopes to pay dividends to its partners for the first time this year, said Munnery. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
